pieces.words: The Jetstream. The same idea you use in Contractors Cloud, in its new home. Tell anyone anything about a customer from the customer's file, and their answer comes back to the same file. Two minutes, for everyone. Step one. Open the customer, from Files, The Line, or the find box. It opens as a drawer. Press Open the full file. Step two. Left side, the customer: their texts and yours. Right side, the team. That is the Jetstream. Nothing you post on the right ever goes to the customer. Step three. Say it in the blue box. To bring someone in, type the at sign and two letters of their name, the way you do in CC. The people come up. Enter, and the name is in your note. Again for the next person, as many as you like. Or one name in the To box: type Eric, it is Eric. Step four. Post, or just press Enter. Everyone you named gets it: a buzz on the phone with the link for a rep or a supervisor, an email with the link for Jess, Sam and Laura. It waits on The Line until they open the file. Nobody else hears about it. Step five. Your note lands in the thread, marked never sent to the customer, with who got it under it. To answer somebody, press Reply on their note: their name fills in, you type, you post. Same customer, in order. No email chain. On the phone, in the 4-Touch app, it is the same thread. Under the texts, tell the team: tap the people, say it, post. When the office tags you, your phone buzzes with the link. Tap it, you are on that file. Answer right there. Three rules. About a customer: on the customer's file. About the day, not one customer: the Village, same at sign. And the customer never sees any of it. Try one today. Open a file, at and two letters, say one thing, Enter. If anything does not work, reply on Kevin's email thread; that thread is the ticket. Nothing to learn. It comes to you.

pieces.words: Sam, Jess, Laura. You asked this morning. Here it is. Six answers, three minutes. One. The New lead door. First name, last name, two boxes, the way Contractors Cloud has them. The file still reads last comma first on its own, so nothing downstream changes. And the address list never says Brevard County for the city any more. If it does not know the city, it leaves it blank and you type it. Two. The customer's file. The phone, the email and the address now sit right under the name. Tap the number to call. Tap the address for the map. Copy any of them with one word. And on the right, new tab: it opens this same file in its own browser tab, so two back to back calls are two tabs, the way you work in CC. Three. The note to the team, on the right side of the file. Type the first letters of a name, Eric, Sam, Obed, and pick. Or type at office, at sales. Nobody scrolls a list. That box is inside only: the customer never sees it, and when your note shows up on the left it is marked inside note, never sent to the customer. You did not text anyone. When is it the Village, and when is it the file? If it is about one customer, it goes on their file and you tag the person. If it is about anything else, it goes in the Village. Either way a tag is a push on their phone and an email with a link to the spot. At rep is the rep on this file: the one who sold it, or the one quoting it. And at supers is every supervisor in every brand, so name the one you mean. Four. Jess asked where a supplier invoice shows up. When Fencing Supply, ABC, Iron World or Havana email you an invoice, the machine reads your mailbox every hour and lands it on the customer's file by the P O number. The Bills tile in the Office room counts what landed. Open the file and the card has Approve on it. Nothing goes to QuickBooks or Contractors Cloud until Kevin flips those switches. Five. Sam's idea, built. In the Office room, a card lists every 811 locate that expires within ten days on a job that has not started. Nothing reorders itself. If the job is on hold, leave it. If it is about to go, reorder it on 811 and the new ticket lands here on its own. Six. Google Calendar. It is built and it is waiting on one permission from Kevin on the Google side. Until he says it is on: type the lead here first, press Copy for CC, type it into Contractors Cloud, press Typed into CC. C C puts it on the rep's Google Calendar the way it always has. Never add it to his calendar by hand; the machine cannot see that and he would get the visit twice. Oasis stays exactly as it is for Mike until Jess says. Tuesday, every new lead starts here. Reply on Kevin's email thread if anything does not work. That thread is the ticket. Nothing to learn. It comes to you.

pieces.title: Every rep · When you miss a call or a text
pieces.what: Kevin, 17 Sep, 4:20 PM: "I have the strangest suspicion that we're missing calls and text." We were. The 15-minute "not answered" notice went only to the watcher and to Kevin, never to the rep; a text on a rep's own number never buzzed the app and landed 15 minutes late; and nobody read the phone company's call list, so 50 calls a day rang out with no one the wiser. Tonight: a customer text on your own number buzzes you when it lands (399); the 15-minute clock buzzes you first and skips ratings, STOP, thank-yous and test files (400); every call sits on the customer's file, and a missed call from a customer buzzes you once (401). Robocalls never buzz. Nothing buzzes 7:30 PM–8 AM. A missed call can show up to an hour late: the list comes once an hour.

ask: What happens when I miss a call or a text?
pieces.words: New tonight. When a customer calls or texts you and you miss it, your phone buzzes. Not Kevin's. Yours. Three things changed. Here they are. One. A customer text on your own number buzzes you the minute it lands. Before tonight it only went on the file, and it got there fifteen minutes late. Two. If a customer text sits fifteen minutes with no answer, the buzz comes to you first. Dana texted, you haven't answered. Kevin only hears about it at sixty. Three. A missed call from a customer buzzes you. Dana called, nobody answered, rang forty seconds on your line at two sixteen. Tap it, the file opens, call back. Every call is on the customer's file now, in the thread with the texts. Answered, placed by you, or missed, in red, with how long it rang. One story, in order. What doesn't buzz. A number that isn't a customer never buzzes you, so the spam stays quiet. A rating, a STOP, a thank-you doesn't start a clock. Nothing buzzes between seven thirty at night and eight in the morning. And one honest note: a missed call can show up to an hour late, because the phone company sends us the list once an hour. That's it. When it buzzes, tap it. The file opens. Text back or call back from there. Nothing to learn. It comes to you.
